newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count up 18 to 808 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count up 18 to 808 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 808 as of September 13, up 18 from the prior week and 49 above the year-ago total of 759, Baker Hughes Inc reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by 17 to 681, while rigs working offshore remained unchanged at 105. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose by one to 22.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in Texas, which showed an increase of 13 and New Mexico, which rose by three. Wyoming dipped by three.

A total of 300 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up seven from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by 11 to 503, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained unchanged at 5.
There were 175 rigs drilling directionally, 64 drilling horizontally and 569 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs dropped by 20 to 240 versus 218 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
